Hi Camila,

We just signed up for Redwood and I wanted to reach out — OpenLib is exploring tighter GitHub integration so our maintainers can trigger/observe model runs directly from PRs and CI. A few quick questions before we book a demo:

- Do you support a GitHub App installation pattern (org-level) vs. personal tokens?

Jordan Peña

Hi Jordan — thanks for the note and welcome to Redwood!

We do have an org-level GitHub App pattern (recommended) — it avoids storing personal tokens and supports repo/org scoping for installations. Typical OAuth scopes are repo/read, admin:repo_hook (for webhook setup), and workflow for CI triggers; I'll loop Alex (our AE) on the call to walk the integration patterns.

I’m free next week on:
- Tue 10/13 10:00–10:30am PT
- Wed 10/14 11:00–11:30am PT
- Thu 10/15 9:00–9:30am PT

Or you can pick a slot on my calendar: https://cal.redwood.ai/book/camila/30

Attaching a short one-pager with our GitHub integration overview. If you have a specific repo or workflow example, send the GitHub issue/PR link and we’ll tailor the demo.

Best,
Camila Reyes

Thanks Jordan — Thu 10/15 at 9:00am PT is great, I’ve booked the 30-minute demo and attached an .ics invite. Alex will join to cover product fit and contract next steps.

Quick answers ahead of the call:
- For webhook setup we recommend read + admin:repo_hook; repo write is not required for standard CI/webhook flows.
- If you plan to run pre-merge checks that write status checks, the GitHub App uses the Checks API (requires checks:write) — we can scope that to specific repos during install.
